strings.issue:NMA-104:title: Cursor pagination skips records when the sort column has duplicate values
strings.issue:NMA-104:desc:0: List endpoints that page with a single-column cursor skip rows when the sort column contains ties. On GET /v2/issues?orderBy=updatedAt&cursor=..., any issues sharing the same updatedAt as the cursor boundary vanish from subsequent pages.
strings.issue:NMA-104:desc:1: Expected: every issue appears exactly once across the full page walk, with stable ordering for ties. Actual: the opaque cursor stores only updatedAt, so the comparison updatedAt > :cursor drops siblings that share that timestamp. A workspace with 40 issues updated in the same millisecond lost 6 of them between page 1 and page 2.
strings.issue:NMA-104:desc:2: Likely cause is the cursor codec encoding a single scalar instead of a composite (updatedAt, id) key. Seek predicates need updatedAt > :ts OR (updatedAt = :ts AND id > :id) with id as the tie-breaker.
strings.issue:NMA-104:desc:3: Integrations that sync the full issue set under-report totals and miss updates. Affects any list route using the shared cursor helper — issues, comments, and projects.
strings.issue:NMA-105:title: Webhook delivery retries exhaust the DLQ without surfacing a final failure event
strings.issue:NMA-105:desc:0: When webhook delivery exhausts its retry budget, the worker parks the message on the DLQ and stops. Subscribers never receive a terminal failure event, so their ops dashboards stay green while deliveries are dead.
strings.issue:NMA-105:desc:1: After the 8th attempt (or the 24-hour retry ceiling), the delivery pipeline should emit webhook.delivery_failed to the subscription's endpoint with the last status code, attempt count, and nextAction=manual_retry. Instead the DLQ write is silent aside from an internal metric.
strings.issue:NMA-105:desc:2: Hypothesis: the failure publisher is only invoked from the synchronous reject path, not from the DLQ admission hook. The async retry chain marks the job terminal without calling emitTerminalFailure.
strings.issue:NMA-105:desc:3: Customers monitoring only their own endpoint miss that Nimbus has given up, and support has no customer-visible trail when asked why events stopped.
strings.issue:NMA-106:title: Rate limiter window resets early under clock skew between API nodes
strings.issue:NMA-106:desc:0: API rate limiter windows reset earlier than the configured 60-second bucket when nodes disagree on wall-clock time. Clients suddenly get a full quota again mid-window, then slam into 429s when traffic lands on a node with a correct clock.
strings.issue:NMA-106:desc:1: Expected behavior is a fixed window anchored to a shared time source so remaining quota decreases monotonically within the window. Observed: under ~180ms skew between api-node-3 and the Redis-backed counter host, local windowStart calculations fall into the prior bucket and refill prematurely.
strings.issue:NMA-106:desc:2: Root hypothesis: each node computes windowStart = floor(localNow / 60s) instead of using Redis TIME or a logical bucket id from the store. Clock skew directly shifts the bucket index.
strings.issue:NMA-106:desc:3: Bursty clients appear to break through limits, then trigger false-positive abuse alerts on the next correctly timed node hop.
strings.issue:NMA-107:title: SDK listIssues ignores the expand=changelog query parameter on v2.4 clients
strings.issue:NMA-107:desc:0: SDK listIssues on the v2.4 client line silently drops expand=changelog. Callers pass the parameter, the HTTP layer builds the query string, but the typed client strips unknown expand tokens before send.
strings.issue:NMA-107:desc:1: Expected: changelog histories return in the expand payload when requested. Actual: the request leaves the SDK without expand, so responses never include histories and apps fall back to N+1 getIssue calls.
strings.issue:NMA-107:desc:2: Likely an allowlist in ExpandParams for v2.4 that never added changelog after the server enabled it in API 2.3. v2.5 clients are fine; only the frozen 2.4 line is affected.
strings.issue:NMA-107:desc:3: Partner integrations pinned to 2.4 show empty activity panels and extra rate-limit pressure from compensatory fetches.
strings.issue:NMA-108:title: Worker crashes when the job payload contains nested null optional fields
strings.issue:NMA-108:desc:0: Export and reindex workers crash hard when a job payload includes nested optional fields explicitly set to null. The panic is a null pointer during struct decode, not a handled validation error.
strings.issue:NMA-108:desc:1: Payloads with nested null optionals should either coerce to omitted or reject with a permanent failure reason. Instead the worker process exits, the job returns to the queue, and the crash loop burns the pod restart budget.
strings.issue:NMA-108:desc:2: Hypothesis: the generated payload structs use nested value types rather than pointers/Option, so unmarshalling cannot represent null and aborts. Top-level nulls are fine; only nested optionals trip it.
strings.issue:NMA-108:desc:3: Long-running export queues stall whenever a client omits a filter by sending null instead of leaving the key out.
strings.issue:NMA-109:title: REST API returns 500 instead of 422 for invalid ISO-8601 due dates
strings.issue:NMA-109:desc:0: POST /v2/issues and PATCH due-date paths return HTTP 500 when the due date string fails ISO-8601 parsing. Clients treat 500 as a platform outage and retry, amplifying load.
strings.issue:NMA-109:desc:1: Invalid values like 2025-13-40 or 2025-04-31T25:00:00Z should yield 422 with a field error on dueDate. Actual response is an unhandled time.Parse panic recovered as a generic 500 with request id only.
strings.issue:NMA-109:desc:2: Cause hypothesis: parseDueDate sits behind the service layer after auth and rate limiting, and its error is not mapped through the validation error type that the HTTP layer turns into 422. Only the happy-path time.Time conversion is tested.
strings.issue:NMA-109:desc:3: SDK users and third-party integrators surface noisy outage alerts for what is simply bad input.
strings.issue:NMA-11:title: audit log ingestion breaks for accounts with more than 1000 records
strings.issue:NMA-11:desc:0: Steps to reproduce: open audit log ingestion with a workspace that has more than one member.
strings.issue:NMA-11:desc:1: Expected: the view keeps the selected filters after a reload.
strings.issue:NMA-11:desc:2: Actual: filters reset to the default and the row count changes.
strings.issue:NMA-11:desc:3: Impact: reported by two customers this week; no data loss observed.
strings.issue:NMA-110:title: Webhook signature header uses the previous secret for 30 seconds after rotation
strings.issue:NMA-110:desc:0: After a webhook secret rotation, the X-Nimbus-Signature header continues to use the previous secret for roughly 30 seconds. Receivers that swapped to the new secret immediately reject those deliveries as invalid.
strings.issue:NMA-110:desc:1: Expected: once rotation commits, new deliveries sign with the new secret; dual-sign (both secrets) may cover a short grace window if documented. Actual: a cache on the signing path keeps the old secret until its 30-second TTL expires, with no dual-sign.
strings.issue:NMA-110:desc:2: Hypothesis: secret material is cached in the delivery worker with key sub:{id}:signing without a publish-time invalidation. Rotation updates Postgres but not the cache, so the worker keeps HMAC-ing with the stale value until TTL.
strings.issue:NMA-110:desc:3: Security-conscious customers who rotate after a leak see a burst of signature failures and may disable the subscription.
strings.issue:NMA-111:title: Rate limit headers omit Retry-After on 429 responses from the edge layer
strings.issue:NMA-111:desc:0: When the edge layer returns 429, response headers include X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining but omit Retry-After. Clients that rely on Retry-After for backoff fall back to blind exponential retries and worsen thundering herds.
strings.issue:NMA-111:desc:1: Expected: 429 responses carry Retry-After as integer seconds until window reset, consistent with the origin API. Actual: only origin-built 429s include it; the edge enforcer synthesizes 429s without copying the reset delta.
strings.issue:NMA-111:desc:2: Likely gap: the edge template for quota denial sets limit/remaining from the redis counter but never computes resetAt - now for Retry-After. Origin and edge header maps diverged when edge rate limiting shipped.
strings.issue:NMA-111:desc:3: Official SDKs already honor Retry-After; without it they retry as early as 200ms and trip secondary limits.
strings.issue:NMA-112:title: SDK webhook verifier fails for payloads larger than 256 KiB
strings.issue:NMA-112:desc:0: The SDK webhook verifier throws or returns invalid signature for bodies larger than 256 KiB even when the HMAC is correct. Large issue.updated payloads with big description fields fail verification every time.
strings.issue:NMA-112:desc:1: Expected: any body within the platform's 1 MiB webhook cap verifies if the signature matches. Actual: the verifier reads the stream into a 256 KiB buffer and either truncates or errors before computing the digest, so the signature never matches the full body.
strings.issue:NMA-112:desc:2: Hypothesis: a hard-coded maxBodyVerify = 256 << 10 in the SDK verifier predates the platform raising the webhook body limit to 1 MiB. Server-side signing uses the full body; client-side checks a prefix.
strings.issue:NMA-112:desc:3: Customers with rich-text heavy projects cannot validate webhooks without a custom verifier.
strings.issue:NMA-113:title: Bulk update endpoint accepts mixed project keys and partially commits changes
strings.issue:NMA-113:desc:0: POST /v2/issues/bulk-update accepts a batch whose issue keys span multiple projects and applies updates to the subset the caller can write, committing partial success without an error envelope. Callers believe the whole batch applied.
strings.issue:NMA-113:desc:1: Expected: either reject the batch with 400 when project keys mix under a single-project token, or return a per-item result set with committed/failed flags. Actual: the handler filters unauthorized or cross-project items silently and returns 200 with only the committed ids in the response body, omitting failures.
strings.issue:NMA-113:desc:2: Hypothesis: authorization is applied per item after the transaction starts, and failed items are skipped without accumulating a failure list. The outer transaction still commits successful rows.
strings.issue:NMA-113:desc:3: Automation scripts that move status across a program of projects end up with half-applied migrations and no signal to retry the rest.
strings.issue:NMA-114:title: Worker heartbeat expires while a long-running export holds the same lease
strings.issue:NMA-114:desc:0: Long-running export jobs hold a worker lease that is also used for heartbeats. When export CPU work blocks the event loop past the 30-second heartbeat interval, the lease expires and another worker picks up the same job.
strings.issue:NMA-114:desc:1: Expected: heartbeat continues for the lifetime of the lease holder, independent of export progress, or export work yields often enough to pump heartbeats. Actual: a single synchronous export of a 2M-row workspace blocks for ~90s; the coordinator expires the lease at 30s and redelivers; two workers write partial export files.
strings.issue:NMA-114:desc:2: Hypothesis: heartbeat ticks run on the same goroutine/event loop as DoExport and never fire while the CPU-heavy encode loop runs. Separate heartbeat thread or lease extension checkpoints inside the encode loop are missing.
strings.issue:NMA-114:desc:3: Duplicate exports waste storage and occasionally upload truncated CSVs to the customer bucket.
strings.issue:NMA-115:title: REST search returns stale results for 45 seconds after an issue is reassigned
strings.issue:NMA-115:desc:0: REST search continues to return the previous assignee for ~45 seconds after an issue is reassigned. Filters on the new assignee miss the issue; filters on the old one still hit it.
strings.issue:NMA-115:desc:1: Expected: search reflects reassignment by the time the update API returns 200, or within the documented near-real-time window of a few seconds. Actual: the search index document keeps the stale assignee until a 45-second refresh cycle, and the update path does not trigger an eager reindex.
strings.issue:NMA-115:desc:2: Hypothesis: issue update publishes to the search indexer over a debounced queue with maxWaitMs=45000, and assignee-only patches are classified as low priority so they always wait for maxWait rather than flushing early.
strings.issue:NMA-115:desc:3: Agents sorting queues by assignee see ghost work and miss newly assigned tickets during that window.
strings.issue:NMA-116:title: Webhook subscription list endpoint ignores the pageSize parameter above 50
strings.issue:NMA-116:desc:0: GET /v2/webhook-subscriptions ignores pageSize when the value is above 50. Clients requesting pageSize=100 still receive at most 50 items with no indication the parameter was clamped.
strings.issue:NMA-116:desc:1: Expected: either honor pageSize up to the documented max of 100, or return 400 when out of range. Actual: the handler silently min(pageSize, 50) because an old constant MaxPageSize=50 was never raised when the public docs moved to 100.
strings.issue:NMA-116:desc:2: Likely a mismatch between the OpenAPI maximum and the hard-coded clamp in listSubscriptions. Cursor generation still works, so clients must issue extra round-trips without knowing why.
strings.issue:NMA-116:desc:3: Large workspaces with many subscriptions take twice the calls to list them all.
strings.issue:NMA-117:title: Rate limiting counts OPTIONS preflight requests against the client quota
strings.issue:NMA-117:desc:0: CORS preflight OPTIONS requests count against the same rate-limit quota as the real API calls. Browser apps that preflight frequently burn through the client's budget before the meaningful methods run.
strings.issue:NMA-117:desc:1: Expected: OPTIONS for CORS is exempt from application quota (or billed to a separate generous bucket). Actual: each preflight decrements the same redis counter keyed by API token, so a chatty SPA can 429 on GET after a burst of OPTIONS alone.
strings.issue:NMA-117:desc:2: Hypothesis: the rate-limit middleware runs before the CORS short-circuit, so OPTIONS never hits the bypass branch that skips quota for health checks. Method allowlisting for quota exemption omits OPTIONS.
strings.issue:NMA-117:desc:3: Browser integrations look flaky under load tests even when server-side call volume is modest.
strings.issue:NMA-118:title: SDK createIssue drops custom field values when the field is multi-select
strings.issue:NMA-118:desc:0: SDK createIssue drops values for multi-select custom fields. The field is present in the request object, but the serialized payload either omits it or sends an empty array, so the issue is created without those selections.
strings.issue:NMA-118:desc:1: Expected: multi-select custom fields accept an array of option ids and persist them on create. Actual: the v2 serializer treats multi-select like single-select and takes only a string path; arrays fail the type guard and the field is stripped before the HTTP send.
strings.issue:NMA-118:desc:2: Hypothesis: CustomFieldValue union in the SDK still models multi-select as string rather than string[], a leftover from when the API only allowed single values. Server API has accepted arrays since 2.2.
strings.issue:NMA-118:desc:3: Migration scripts and intake forms that set multi-select metadata create incomplete issues and require manual edits.
strings.issue:NMA-119:title: Worker dead-letter requeue loses the original attempt count metadata
strings.issue:NMA-119:desc:0: When a job exhausts its delivery budget and lands in the dead-letter queue, the requeue path rebuilds the envelope from the DLQ record alone. Operators who then push the job back onto the live queue see attempt_count reset to 0 even though the DLQ row still holds attempt_count=7 and first_failed_at from the original run.
strings.issue:NMA-119:desc:1: Expected requeue to copy attempt_count, max_attempts, and first_failed_at into the new queue message so downstream dashboards and circuit-breaker logic keep continuity. Actual behavior only restores job_id, payload, and topic; the attempt fields are re-initialized by the publisher defaults.
strings.issue:NMA-119:desc:2: Suspected cause: dlq_requeue() serializes a fresh JobHeader via DefaultHeader() instead of unmarshaling the stored header blob, so the attempt metadata never leaves cold storage. Impact is skewed retry metrics and premature permanent-failure classification on the second cycle after requeue.
strings.issue:NMA-12:title: Add integration tests for token refresh
strings.issue:NMA-12:desc:0: Context: Add integration tests for token refresh.
strings.issue:NMA-12:desc:1: Acceptance: behaviour is covered by a test and documented in the reference.
strings.issue:NMA-120:title: REST API CORS allowlist rejects legitimate subdomains of example.com
strings.issue:NMA-120:desc:0: Clients calling https://api.tenant.example.com from https://app.tenant.example.com receive a CORS rejection even though *.example.com was added to the allowlist in the admin console. Preflight OPTIONS succeeds for the apex host but fails for any multi-label subdomain under the same registered domain.
strings.issue:NMA-120:desc:1: The matcher splits the Origin host on dots and only compares the final two labels against each allowlist entry. That treats app.tenant.example.com as unrelated to an entry of example.com or *.example.com when the rule was stored without an explicit leading wildcard token.
strings.issue:NMA-120:desc:2: Expectation is that an allowlist entry of example.com (or *.example.com) covers every subdomain depth under that registrable domain. Actual responses include Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing and a console error on the SPA bootstrap call to GET /v2/me.
strings.issue:NMA-120:desc:3: Likely bug is in cors.MatchOrigin: it uses strings.HasSuffix against a single-dot suffix instead of publicsuffix-aware suffix matching, so three-or-more label hosts never pass.
strings.issue:NMA-121:title: Webhook test delivery endpoint always returns 200 even when the target is down
strings.issue:NMA-121:desc:0: POST /v2/webhooks/{id}/test always responds with HTTP 200 and body {"delivered": true} regardless of whether the configured target URL is reachable. Pointing a subscription at https://hooks.example.com/unreachable still yields the success envelope within ~40ms.
strings.issue:NMA-121:desc:1: Product expectation for the test endpoint is to perform a real signed POST, wait up to the 8s delivery timeout, and return the upstream status code plus our delivery_id. Operators currently cannot distinguish a healthy target from a dead one without tailing worker logs.
strings.issue:NMA-121:desc:2: The handler appears to enqueue a fire-and-forget DeliveryJob and return before the worker reports outcome. Response mapping never inspects delivery_attempts.last_status, so the HTTP layer hard-codes 200.
strings.issue:NMA-121:desc:3: Affects onboarding: new integrations mark the connection green even when the partner endpoint is misconfigured, delaying real incident discovery until the first production event fails.
strings.issue:NMA-122:title: Pagination total count drifts when filters include labels with special characters
strings.issue:NMA-122:desc:0: Listing issues with a label filter that contains plus, slash, or unicode punctuation returns a page of items whose length does not match the total field. Example: label=ci/cd+nightly yields 12 rows on page 1 but total=0, while the unfiltered count for the same project is 847.
strings.issue:NMA-122:desc:1: The count query URL-decodes the label once before binding, but the data query goes through a second decode in the filter builder. Labels with reserved characters end up as different strings in the two SQL paths, so COUNT(*) and the LIMIT/OFFSET select disagree.
strings.issue:NMA-122:desc:2: Clients that drive progress bars from total then show empty or complete states incorrectly. Workaround is to omit total and page until the last empty page, which is expensive for large projects.
strings.issue:NMA-123:title: SDK retry middleware does not honor 503 Retry-After delay values
strings.issue:NMA-123:desc:0: The official SDK retry middleware treats any 503 as a signal to apply the configured exponential backoff (base 250ms, cap 4s) and ignores the Retry-After header when the server sends a delta-seconds value. Under coordinated maintenance we emit Retry-After: 12, yet the client still hammers /v2/search every few hundred milliseconds.
strings.issue:NMA-123:desc:1: Spec for the middleware says numeric Retry-After must set the next sleep to at least that many seconds before the usual jitter. Observed sleeps stay under 1s across five consecutive 503s in the integration harness.
strings.issue:NMA-123:desc:2: Hypothesis: parseRetryAfter only handles HTTP-date form and returns zero for pure integers, after which the backoff branch never substitutes the server hint. Reopened after 1.9.2 claimed a fix — the unit test only covered the HTTP-date branch.
strings.issue:NMA-123:desc:3: Customers with aggressive concurrency see amplified 503 storms and longer outages when we intentionally shed load.
strings.issue:NMA-124:title: Worker concurrency semaphore leaks slots after a panicked handler
strings.issue:NMA-124:desc:0: A handler that panics during Execute leaves the concurrency semaphore permanently acquired. After roughly 64 panics on a worker with max_inflight=64, the process stops accepting new jobs while CPU and memory look idle and the lease renewer is still healthy.
strings.issue:NMA-124:desc:1: Expected path: recover in the outer run loop releases the slot via defer, then records the panic to the DLQ. Actual path acquires the weighted semaphore before installing the recover defer, so a panic between acquire and defer registration (or inside a non-deferred unlock helper) never returns the weight.
strings.issue:NMA-124:desc:2: Root cause was acquireSlot() returning a release func that callers were expected to defer, but the panic wrapper called release only on the success and error returns — not on recover. Once max_inflight slots leaked, only a process restart restored throughput.
strings.issue:NMA-124:desc:3: Hit overnight on the media-thumbnail pool after a nil-pointer regression in an image library upgrade.
strings.issue:NMA-125:title: REST field metadata endpoint caches deleted custom fields for the full TTL
strings.issue:NMA-125:desc:0: GET /v2/field-metadata continues to list custom fields for up to the full 15-minute cache TTL after an admin deletes them. Clients that cache the response themselves then show pickers for fields that return 404 on write.
strings.issue:NMA-125:desc:1: Delete handler removes the row from custom_fields but only busts the per-project key fieldmeta:{project_id}. Global and workspace-scoped entries fieldmeta:ws:{id} keep serving the pre-delete snapshot until natural expiry.
strings.issue:NMA-125:desc:2: Reopened because the first fix busted project keys only; workspace-level metadata used by multi-project boards still served ghosts for the remaining TTL. Expectation is immediate consistency on delete for every cache key that included that field_id.
strings.issue:NMA-126:title: Rate limiter redis key collision occurs across staging and production clusters
strings.issue:NMA-126:desc:0: Staging and production API clusters share a Redis logical database for historical reasons and form rate-limit keys as rl:{api_key_hash}:{window}. A load test in staging that exhausts a key hash identical to a production token shape can throttle real traffic if the hash collides, and staging resets have cleared production counters overnight.
strings.issue:NMA-126:desc:1: Keys must be cluster-scoped (e.g. rl:{env}:{api_key_hash}:{window}) or use separate Redis DBs. Today neither env var RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX nor the deployment name is folded into the key material.
strings.issue:NMA-126:desc:2: During last Thursday's staging soak we observed production 429 rates jump ~3x for tokens whose SHA-256 prefix matched fixtures in the load script. No data corruption, but customer-facing throttling from a non-prod workload is unacceptable.
strings.issue:NMA-127:title: Webhook payload omits the previous status when the transition skips intermediate states
strings.issue:NMA-127:desc:0: When an issue jumps from To Do straight to Done via a workflow transition that skips In Progress, the issue.updated webhook body sets status to Done but leaves previous_status null (or omits the field). Consumers that drive automations on status deltas cannot tell what the prior state was.
strings.issue:NMA-127:desc:1: Normal single-step transitions correctly populate previous_status from the transition's from_status_id. Multi-hop or admin "move to" paths load only the destination status into the event builder and never read issues.status before the update commit.
strings.issue:NMA-127:desc:2: Hypothesis: StatusTransitionEvent is built after the UPDATE, and the skip path uses a bulk status writer that does not pass old_status into the outbox payload. Fix should snapshot status in the same transaction before write, regardless of intermediate skips.
strings.issue:NMA-127:desc:3: Integrations that gate on leaving In Progress silently no-op for these jumps, which is how the report surfaced.
strings.issue:NMA-128:title: SDK TypeScript types mark required create fields as optional after codegen
strings.issue:NMA-128:desc:0: After running the OpenAPI codegen for SDK 2.1, TypeScript interfaces for create payloads mark project_key, summary, and issue_type as optional even though the API returns 400 without them. Call sites that relied on compile-time required checks now type-check with empty objects.
strings.issue:NMA-128:desc:1: The generator maps all schema properties through a nullable-union helper that strips required[] when any property uses allOf wrappers. CreateIssueRequest is defined with allOf + required, and the helper drops the required list while merging.
strings.issue:NMA-128:desc:2: Expectation: fields listed in the OpenAPI required array remain non-optional in the emitted .d.ts. Actual: every create body field is T | undefined, so strict clients ship incomplete requests that only fail at runtime.
strings.issue:NMA-129:title: Worker job IDs collide when two nodes boot within the same millisecond
strings.issue:NMA-129:desc:0: Job IDs are composed as {node_id_hex}-{millis_since_epoch}-{counter}. When two worker nodes finish boot in the same millisecond and both start counters at 0, the first jobs they enqueue can share an identical job_id if node_id assignment also collides during a brief membership flap.
strings.issue:NMA-129:desc:1: More commonly, node_id is derived from a truncated MAC hash that collides under certain cloud NIC renames, so the millisecond+counter pair alone is not unique. Duplicate primary keys on job_events then cause the second insert to fail and the job to be dropped after the publish ack.
strings.issue:NMA-129:desc:2: A safer scheme would use a 128-bit random id or include a process start ulid segment that is unique per process lifetime. Current collision window is small but has produced at least three lost jobs in the last 30 days on the EU pool.
strings.issue:NMA-13:title: token refresh throws 500 when the workspace has no members
strings.issue:NMA-13:desc:0: Steps to reproduce: open token refresh with a workspace that has more than one member.
strings.issue:NMA-13:desc:1: Expected: the view keeps the selected filters after a reload.
strings.issue:NMA-13:desc:2: Actual: filters reset to the default and the row count changes.
strings.issue:NMA-13:desc:3: Impact: reported by two customers this week; no data loss observed.
strings.issue:NMA-130:title: REST API accepts empty assignee_slot strings instead of returning 400
strings.issue:NMA-130:desc:0: PUT /v2/issues/{id} accepts assignee_slot: "" and stores an empty string instead of rejecting the body. Downstream assignment UIs treat empty string as a distinct slot from null, showing a blank chip that cannot be cleared without a raw API call.
strings.issue:NMA-130:desc:1: Validation already rejects whitespace-only display names and unknown slot tokens, but the empty string bypasses the enum check because the binder coerces "" to a present optional before the non-empty rule runs.
strings.issue:NMA-130:desc:2: Expected: 400 with code field_invalid and message that assignee_slot must be a non-empty slot id or omitted/null to unassign. Actual: 200 with assignee_slot saved as "".
strings.issue:NMA-131:title: Webhook fan-out delivers events twice when the subscription uses two endpoints
strings.issue:NMA-131:desc:0: A single webhook subscription configured with two endpoint URLs receives each event twice on both endpoints (four HTTP deliveries total) instead of once per endpoint. Fan-out should produce N deliveries for N endpoints, not N×N.
strings.issue:NMA-131:desc:1: The dispatcher iterates endpoints and, for each, reloads the full endpoint list from the subscription snapshot before enqueue. Nested iteration multiplies the set: with 2 endpoints the inner loop runs twice per outer step.
strings.issue:NMA-131:desc:2: Discovered via partner logs showing duplicate delivery_id pairs differing only by a trailing endpoint index that was applied twice. No data loss on our side, but partner automations double-executed.
strings.issue:NMA-132:title: Expose a public endpoint to list webhook delivery attempts for a subscription
strings.issue:NMA-132:desc:0: Support and integrators currently need internal admin tools or log access to inspect whether a given webhook subscription delivered, retried, or exhausted a specific event. That slows incident response when a partner claims they never received issue.updated.
strings.issue:NMA-132:desc:1: Expose GET /v2/webhooks/{subscription_id}/deliveries with filters for event_type, status (success|failed|pending), and created_after. Each item should include attempt_number, http_status, latency_ms, response_snippet (truncated), and next_retry_at.
strings.issue:NMA-132:desc:2: Acceptance: a project admin token can list the last 7 days of attempts for subscriptions they own; responses are paginated with cursor; secrets and full response bodies are never returned; rate limited to 30 req/min per token.
strings.issue:NMA-133:title: Allow SDK consumers to stream search results via async iterators
strings.issue:NMA-133:desc:0: Large search result sets force SDK users to hand-roll offset or cursor loops, which is error-prone around rate limits and cancellation. Native async iteration would match how many runtimes already consume streams.
strings.issue:NMA-133:desc:1: Add client.issues.searchStream(query) that yields Issue objects via AsyncIterable, internally advancing the cursor from each page's next_cursor until exhausted or the abort signal fires.
strings.issue:NMA-133:desc:2: Acceptance: works in Node 18+ and modern browsers; respects the client's retry middleware; documents backpressure as best-effort (pull-based); unit tests cover empty pages, single page, and mid-stream 429 recovery.
strings.issue:NMA-134:title: Support soft rate-limit warnings at 80 percent of the hourly quota
strings.issue:NMA-134:desc:0: Hard 429s at 100% of the hourly quota surprise clients that could have shed load earlier. Several partners asked for a predictive signal before the hard ceiling.
strings.issue:NMA-134:desc:1: When usage crosses 80% of the hourly budget, include RateLimit-Warning: 80-percent with remaining and reset timestamps on otherwise successful responses. Do not change status codes or body shapes.
strings.issue:NMA-134:desc:2: Acceptance: warning appears only on authenticated routes that already emit RateLimit-Remaining; warning clears after the window rolls; documented in the public rate-limit guide; feature-flagged for a one-week canary.
strings.issue:NMA-135:title: Let workers publish progress checkpoints for multi-minute export jobs
strings.issue:NMA-135:desc:0: Multi-minute CSV/JSON exports leave the UI with a spinner and no intermediate feedback. Support tickets spike when users refresh and start a second export.
strings.issue:NMA-135:desc:1: Workers writing export jobs may POST progress checkpoints {percent, rows_done, rows_estimated, updated_at} to an internal progress channel every ~5 seconds or every 2k rows, whichever comes first. The jobs API surfaces the latest checkpoint on GET /v2/jobs/{id}.
strings.issue:NMA-135:desc:2: Acceptance: a 500k-row export updates percent at least 10 times before completion; failed jobs retain the last checkpoint; checkpoints older than 24h are pruned with the job row.
strings.issue:NMA-136:title: Add a REST filter for issues updated since a specific cursor token
strings.issue:NMA-136:desc:0: Sync agents that poll for recently changed issues currently approximate "since" with updated_at timestamps, which misses clock skew and double-delivers rows updated in the same second.
strings.issue:NMA-136:desc:1: Add query parameter updated_since_cursor on GET /v2/issues that accepts an opaque token returned from a previous page or from X-Issues-Cursor on list responses. Server decodes to a (updated_at, issue_id) pair for stable keyset pagination.
strings.issue:NMA-136:desc:2: Acceptance: cursor is monotonic across concurrent updates; invalid tokens return 400; documentation includes a sample poll loop; works with existing project and label filters.
strings.issue:NMA-137:title: Provide signed temporary URLs for large attachment downloads in the SDK
strings.issue:NMA-137:desc:0: Attachment download currently streams through the API gateway, which caps throughput and holds worker connections for multi-hundred-MB files. Edge and mobile clients need a short-lived direct URL.
strings.issue:NMA-137:desc:1: SDK method attachments.getDownloadUrl(id, {ttlSeconds}) should call a new REST route that returns a signed HTTPS URL valid between 60 and 900 seconds, plus content_type and byte_size.
strings.issue:NMA-137:desc:2: Acceptance: URL requires no API key at the storage edge; revoked attachments fail with 404 on sign; SDK throws on ttl outside range; documented threat model notes that anyone with the URL can download until expiry.
strings.issue:NMA-138:title: Allow webhook filters by project key and issue type without a separate subscription
strings.issue:NMA-138:desc:0: Teams that only care about bugs in project ALPHA currently create separate subscriptions or filter in their own service. That multiplies secrets and delivery noise for high-volume workspaces.
strings.issue:NMA-138:desc:1: Allow a single subscription to declare include_project_keys and include_issue_types arrays. Events that fail the filter are dropped before fan-out and do not count against delivery quota.
strings.issue:NMA-138:desc:2: Acceptance: empty arrays mean no restriction; unknown project keys rejected at write time; changing filters does not drop in-flight deliveries; OpenAPI and webhook console UI updated together.
strings.issue:NMA-139:title: Surface remaining rate-limit budget on every successful authenticated response
strings.issue:NMA-139:desc:0: Clients today only learn remaining budget when they finally hit 429 or when they call a separate quota endpoint. Embedding budget on success responses lets them pace batches without extra round-trips.
strings.issue:NMA-139:desc:1: On every successful authenticated response, emit RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset (unix seconds) consistent with the hourly window that applied to that route class.
strings.issue:NMA-139:desc:2: Acceptance: header values match the Redis counter within one request of race; unauthenticated public GETs omit the headers; changelog entry and SDK response wrapper expose remaining as a number.

strings.issue:NMA-14:desc:0: Context: Document bulk import worker in the public reference.
strings.issue:NMA-14:desc:1: Acceptance: behaviour is covered by a test and documented in the reference.
strings.issue:NMA-140:title: Add a dry-run mode for bulk mutation endpoints that returns a change plan
strings.issue:NMA-140:desc:0: Bulk edit and bulk transition endpoints are hard to validate safely against production-shaped data. Partners want a preview of what would change without committing writes.
strings.issue:NMA-140:desc:1: Support dry_run=true on POST /v2/issues/bulk-update and /v2/issues/bulk-transition. Response returns a change plan: matched_count, would_update_count, sample of up to 20 issue ids with before/after field snapshots, and validation errors per id — no row mutations, no webhooks.
strings.issue:NMA-140:desc:2: Acceptance: dry_run requests do not increment write audit logs as mutations; authorization is identical to the real path; plan generation finishes within 5s for up to 500 matched issues.
strings.issue:NMA-141:title: Let SDK clients configure a custom fetch implementation for edge runtimes
strings.issue:NMA-141:desc:0: Edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy) cannot use the default global fetch binding the SDK closes over at module init, or they need undici-compatible stubs with custom cert handling.
strings.issue:NMA-141:desc:1: Allow NimbusClient options.fetch to supply any fetch-compatible function; all HTTP calls in the SDK must go through that hook, including retries and streaming helpers.
strings.issue:NMA-141:desc:2: Acceptance: documented example for a custom fetch; default remains globalThis.fetch; type definitions accept typeof fetch; integration test injects a mock that records URLs.
strings.issue:NMA-142:title: Support idempotency keys on create endpoints for at-most-once client retries
strings.issue:NMA-142:desc:0: Mobile and flaky networks often retry POST /v2/issues and create duplicates when the first request succeeded but the response was lost. Clients need at-most-once semantics without building their own dedupe store.
strings.issue:NMA-142:desc:1: Accept header Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4 recommended) on create endpoints. First request stores the response body and status for 24h keyed by (api_key_id, idempotency_key); replays return the stored response without re-executing side effects.
strings.issue:NMA-142:desc:2: Acceptance: conflicting body hash for the same key returns 409; keys expire after 24h; documented for issues, comments, and webhook subscriptions create routes.
strings.issue:NMA-143:title: Expose worker queue depth metrics via a read-only ops endpoint
strings.issue:NMA-143:desc:0: On-call currently scrapes worker logs or Redis CLI to judge backlog severity. A stable ops signal is needed for dashboards and autoscaling.
strings.issue:NMA-143:desc:1: Add GET /v2/ops/worker-queues (ops-scoped token only) returning per-queue depth, oldest_job_age_seconds, and inflight for each named topic. Read-only, no job payloads.
strings.issue:NMA-143:desc:2: Acceptance: authorized ops tokens only (403 otherwise); p99 latency under 100ms; metrics match Redis LLEN within a 2s skew; runbook updated.
strings.issue:NMA-144:title: Allow partial field updates on issues without replacing the full body
strings.issue:NMA-144:desc:0: PATCH was missing for issues, so clients had to PUT the full resource and risked clobbering concurrent edits to unrelated fields.
strings.issue:NMA-144:desc:1: Support PATCH /v2/issues/{id} with a partial JSON object; only provided fields are validated and written. Unset fields remain unchanged. Use merge semantics for maps like custom_fields (shallow merge by key).
strings.issue:NMA-144:desc:2: Acceptance: patching summary alone does not clear description; unknown fields 400; ETag / If-Match still enforced; OpenAPI and SDK updated.
strings.issue:NMA-145:title: Add SDK helpers for building JQL-like filters with typed field names
strings.issue:NMA-145:desc:0: Hand-built JQL-like filter strings in application code are a common source of escaping bugs and typos on field names.
strings.issue:NMA-145:desc:1: Ship SDK helpers such as filters.and(filters.eq('status', 'Done'), filters.contains('labels', 'backend')) that produce the wire filter AST the search API already accepts, with TypeScript/Python typed field name unions generated from field metadata.
strings.issue:NMA-145:desc:2: Acceptance: helpers cover eq, neq, in, contains, gt/lt on dates; output matches hand-written filters in golden tests; no runtime dependency on a full JQL parser.
strings.issue:NMA-146:title: Support rotating webhook secrets with a dual-validation grace period
strings.issue:NMA-146:desc:0: Rotating a webhook secret today is a hard cutover: partners must update verifiers at the same instant we switch signing keys, which causes signature failures during deploys.
strings.issue:NMA-146:desc:1: Support setting a next_secret while current_secret remains valid. For a configurable grace period (default 48h), deliveries are signed with next_secret and verification on our test endpoint accepts either secret. After grace, current is replaced and next cleared.
strings.issue:NMA-146:desc:2: Acceptance: admin API to begin/commit/cancel rotation; delivery headers include X-Nimbus-Signature-Version so consumers know which key was used; audit log entries for each rotation step.
strings.issue:NMA-147:title: Let API keys be scoped to a subset of projects and HTTP methods
strings.issue:NMA-147:desc:0: Workspace-wide API keys are too broad for contractors and CI jobs that should only touch a few projects or only read.
strings.issue:NMA-147:desc:1: Allow API keys to declare project_ids allowlist and allowed_methods (subset of GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE). Requests outside the scope return 403 with code key_scope_violation.
strings.issue:NMA-147:desc:2: Acceptance: empty project list means all projects (backward compatible); method list required at create; existing keys migrate as unrestricted; admin UI can edit scope without rotating the secret.
strings.issue:NMA-148:title: Provide a bulk reindex endpoint that reports per-project completion status
strings.issue:NMA-148:desc:0: Search index rebuilds after schema changes are triggered per project via support tools. Customers with many projects need a self-serve bulk kickoff and visibility into which projects finished.
strings.issue:NMA-148:desc:1: POST /v2/admin/reindex with project_keys[] (or all=true for workspace admins) enqueues reindex jobs and returns a run_id. GET /v2/admin/reindex/{run_id} lists per-project status: queued, running, done, failed, with counts and error summaries.
strings.issue:NMA-148:desc:2: Acceptance: cannot start a second overlapping all=true run; failed projects are retryable via POST .../retry; progress visible within 10s of worker updates.
strings.issue:NMA-149:title: Allow workers to pause and resume long-running jobs without losing lease state
strings.issue:NMA-149:desc:0: Long export and reindex jobs are sometimes intentionally paused for maintenance windows, but today pause cancels the lease and the job restarts from scratch or is marked failed.
strings.issue:NMA-149:desc:1: Workers should support pause and resume control messages that freeze progress, renew a paused lease with a longer TTL, and on resume continue from the last checkpoint without reprocessing completed partitions.
strings.issue:NMA-149:desc:2: Acceptance: pause is idempotent; resume fails clearly if the checkpoint is missing; paused jobs do not count toward concurrency slots; ops endpoint shows paused state and lease expiry.

strings.issue:NMA-150:title: Add integration tests for the bulk import worker pagination edge cases
strings.issue:NMA-150:desc:0: Bulk import worker pagination has had three production incidents around empty final pages, page sizes larger than remaining rows, and source cursors that rewind after a 503. Coverage today is mostly unit tests on pure helpers.
strings.issue:NMA-150:desc:1: Done when an integration suite spins a fake source API and asserts: empty last page completes the job; mid-stream 503 retries without duplicating imported issue keys; page_size=1 and page_size=500 both reach terminal success; metrics counters for pages_fetched match expectations.
strings.issue:NMA-151:title: Document rate limit tiers and header semantics for public API consumers
strings.issue:NMA-151:desc:0: Public docs mention rate limits only in passing and omit header names, window length, and per-route cost multipliers. Partners reverse-engineer behavior from 429 bodies.
strings.issue:NMA-151:desc:1: Complete when the developer portal has a dedicated page covering free/pro/enterprise hourly tiers, RateLimit-* headers, 429 JSON shape, Retry-After behavior, and cost weights for search vs write routes, reviewed by DX and linked from the API reference.
strings.issue:NMA-152:title: Migrate webhook delivery logs to a partitioned cold-storage table
strings.issue:NMA-152:desc:0: webhook_delivery_logs is a single hot table past 400M rows; vacuum and index maintenance stall writers during peak. Query patterns are almost always time-bounded by created_at.
strings.issue:NMA-152:desc:1: Migrate to monthly range partitions on created_at, detach partitions older than 90 days to cold storage object dumps, and keep a thin hot parent for the recent window. Completion means dual-write validation for one week, cutover runbook executed in staging then production, and app queries unchanged via the parent table name.
strings.issue:NMA-153:title: Generate SDK release notes from the OpenAPI diff for each minor version
strings.issue:NMA-153:desc:0: SDK changelogs were hand-written and often missed OpenAPI-only additions. Consumers need accurate minor-version notes without relying on tribal knowledge.
strings.issue:NMA-153:desc:1: Done when CI on the SDK repo runs an OpenAPI diff against the previous minor tag and generates a markdown release-notes fragment (added/removed/changed operations and schemas) attached to the GitHub release and npm package README section.
strings.issue:NMA-154:title: Instrument REST 4xx/5xx ratios with project-key dimensions
strings.issue:NMA-154:desc:0: REST error traffic is only visible as global counts today, which hides which project keys drive most 4xx and 5xx responses during incidents.
strings.issue:NMA-154:desc:1: Add instrumentation that records 4xx and 5xx ratios with a project-key dimension so on-call can slice dashboards by tenant without replaying logs.
strings.issue:NMA-154:desc:2: Keep cardinality bounded by hashing unknown keys into an other bucket and document the metric names for the platform observability wiki.
strings.issue:NMA-155:title: Replace ad-hoc sleep retries with the shared exponential backoff package
strings.issue:NMA-155:desc:0: Several SDK modules still retry network failures with fixed Thread.sleep loops that ignore jitter and total deadline budgets.
strings.issue:NMA-155:desc:1: Replace those ad-hoc sleeps with the shared exponential backoff package already used by the CLI so retry policy stays consistent across languages.
strings.issue:NMA-155:desc:2: Preserve existing public retry hook callbacks and add a unit test that proves backoff doubles up to the configured ceiling.
strings.issue:NMA-156:title: Add contract tests for webhook signature verification across secret rotations
strings.issue:NMA-156:desc:0: Webhook signature verification is covered by happy-path unit tests only, so secret rotation windows are untested.
strings.issue:NMA-156:desc:1: Add contract tests that rotate signing secrets mid-suite, accept requests signed with the previous secret within the grace period, and reject them after expiry.
strings.issue:NMA-156:desc:2: Cover both HMAC header styles we document for external partners on example.com callback endpoints.
strings.issue:NMA-157:title: Backfill missing created_at indexes on the worker job history table
strings.issue:NMA-157:desc:0: The worker job history table lacks created_at indexes on several shards, so retention cleanup scans full partitions during peak hours.
strings.issue:NMA-157:desc:1: Backfill the missing indexes online with a throttled migration that pauses when replica lag exceeds the agreed threshold.
strings.issue:NMA-157:desc:2: Validate query plans for the cleanup job and the history browser after each shard completes.
strings.issue:NMA-158:title: Remove deprecated v1 list endpoints still referenced in internal docs
strings.issue:NMA-158:desc:0: Deprecated v1 list endpoints remain registered for compatibility even though public clients moved to v2 months ago.
strings.issue:NMA-158:desc:1: Remove the handlers, update internal docs that still deep-link to the old paths, and return a clear gone response only if any residual traffic appears.

strings.issue:NMA-159:title: Add chaos tests for rate limiter redis failover behavior
strings.issue:NMA-159:desc:0: Rate limiter behavior during Redis failover is only verified manually after incidents.
strings.issue:NMA-159:desc:1: Add chaos tests that kill the primary Redis node mid-burst and assert fail-open versus fail-closed modes match configuration for each limiter class.
strings.issue:NMA-159:desc:2: Record recovery time and duplicate allow decisions so we can set SLOs for the rate limiting control plane.

strings.issue:NMB-104:title: Filter chips reset to default after switching workspaces
strings.issue:NMB-104:desc:0: On the main dashboard, chip filters (status, assignee, component) are remembered while you stay in one workspace. After you change workspace from the top switcher, every chip snaps back to the product default set even though the prior selection was still valid for that board.
strings.issue:NMB-104:desc:1: Expected: each workspace keeps its own chip selection for the browser session, or at least restores the last filters stored under that workspace id. Actual: the chip bar always reloads from DEFAULT_FILTERS after a workspace change, discarding custom combinations of three or more chips.
strings.issue:NMB-104:desc:2: Suspect the filter store keys only on userId and never includes workspaceId, so the hydrate path after workspace.switched overwrites local state with the global default map. Users who juggle two or three workspaces re-apply the same chips dozens of times per day and lose the filtered board context mid-review.
strings.issue:NMB-105:title: Dashboard chart legend overlaps axis labels on 1280px viewports
strings.issue:NMB-105:desc:0: Throughput charts on the overview dashboard look fine at 1440px and above. At exactly 1280px wide (common laptop layout with the left nav open), the legend pills sit on top of the Y-axis tick labels and make both unreadable.
strings.issue:NMB-105:desc:1: You should still be able to read every tick and every series name without overlap. What happens is the legend is absolutely positioned against the chart container while the axis padding stays fixed at 32px, so once the plot area shrinks the two regions collide.
strings.issue:NMB-105:desc:2: Likely the chart layout pass computes legend height after axis margins are locked, instead of reserving space first. Support has two tickets from teams that live on 13-inch displays and cannot read weekly velocity at that breakpoint.
strings.issue:NMB-106:title: Billing invoice PDF downloads with a blank second page
strings.issue:NMB-106:desc:0: Monthly invoice PDFs generated from Billing → Invoices open correctly on page one (header, line items, totals) but always include a second page that is completely blank except for the footer page number.
strings.issue:NMB-106:desc:1: A single-page invoice should produce a single-page PDF. Accounting users who archive invoices into their ERPs end up with empty pages that their OCR tools flag as corrupt or incomplete.
strings.issue:NMB-106:desc:2: Hypothesis: the PDF renderer always appends a page-break after the totals block because the template still contains a residual page-break-after: always on .invoice-totals from when multi-page tax schedules were required. Removing that rule or gating it on content height over 720pt should drop the empty page.
strings.issue:NMB-107:title: Auth session cookie is not refreshed after silent token renewal
strings.issue:NMB-107:desc:0: Silent access-token renewal succeeds (network tab shows 200 from /auth/token/refresh with a new expires_at), yet the session cookie nimbus_sid keeps its original Max-Age and Expires values from the first login.
strings.issue:NMB-107:desc:1: After renewal the cookie should be re-issued with a sliding window matching the new token lifetime. Instead the browser keeps the old cookie; once that clock runs out the next navigation returns 401 even though a valid access token still sits in memory.
strings.issue:NMB-107:desc:2: Root cause candidate: the refresh handler updates the in-memory JWT store but never calls Set-Cookie on the response when the grant type is refresh_token. Only the interactive login path sets the cookie. Users on long-lived tabs hit sudden logouts about 12 hours after the first sign-in despite continuous silent renewals.
strings.issue:NMB-108:title: Notification toast stacks behind the sticky editor toolbar
strings.issue:NMB-108:desc:0: When the sticky editor toolbar is pinned (scrollY > 64), success and error toasts from save, share, and permission actions render underneath the toolbar instead of above it. Clicks on toast actions never register because the toolbar captures pointer events.
strings.issue:NMB-108:desc:1: Toasts should sit in a layer above chrome UI. Currently toast z-index is 40 while the sticky toolbar uses 50, so any toast that appears near the top of the viewport is fully or partially obscured.
strings.issue:NMB-108:desc:2: Stacking context is created by the toolbar's position: sticky plus transform used for the shadow fade. Raising the toast portal to z-index 60 (or moving it outside the editor stacking root) should fix it. Missed confirmations are especially painful on failed share invites where the error is invisible.
strings.issue:NMB-109:title: Editor autosave writes the previous document revision every third save
strings.issue:NMB-109:desc:0: Editor autosave should always persist the latest document body. On every third successful autosave (approximately every 90 seconds with default debounce), the payload sent to PUT /docs/{id}/revisions contains the body from the previous revision instead of the live editor state.
strings.issue:NMB-109:desc:1: Expected: each autosave captures the current ProseMirror doc. Actual: saves 1 and 2 are correct; save 3 rewrites the server copy with revision N-1 content, wiping the intervening edits until the next good save.
strings.issue:NMB-109:desc:2: Cause was a ring buffer of size 2 in AutosaveQueue that rotated the wrong index when flush and enqueue raced after a 2s idle. The third flush reused the stale snapshot reference. Fix re-reads view.state.doc at flush time instead of caching the JSON string at enqueue.
strings.issue:NMB-109:desc:3: Impact was silent data loss for anyone typing through multiple autosave cycles; several writers reported that their last paragraph vanished after returning from a short break.
strings.issue:NMB-11:title: SSO callback loses state after a browser refresh
strings.issue:NMB-11:desc:0: Steps to reproduce: open SSO callback with a workspace that has more than one member.
strings.issue:NMB-11:desc:1: Expected: the view keeps the selected filters after a reload.
strings.issue:NMB-11:desc:2: Actual: filters reset to the default and the row count changes.
strings.issue:NMB-11:desc:3: Impact: reported by two customers this week; no data loss observed.
strings.issue:NMB-110:title: Workspace switcher shows stale plan tier until full page reload
strings.issue:NMB-110:desc:0: The workspace switcher dropdown shows the plan tier badge (Free, Team, Business) next to each workspace name. After an admin upgrades or downgrades a workspace, the badge in the switcher keeps showing the old tier until the user does a full browser reload.
strings.issue:NMB-110:desc:1: Plan changes should surface within a few seconds of the billing webhook completing. In practice the switcher reads from a bootstrap payload cached at login and never refetches GET /workspaces/me after workspace.plan_changed.
strings.issue:NMB-110:desc:2: Stale tier text causes people to open the wrong upgrade CTA or believe a paid feature is unavailable. Caching the tier on the workspace list without a subscription to plan events is the likely gap.
strings.issue:NMB-111:title: Dark mode contrast fails WCAG AA on secondary dashboard metrics
strings.issue:NMB-111:desc:0: In dark theme, secondary dashboard metrics (cycle time subtitle, percentile footnotes, compared-to-last-period deltas) use #8B8B9A on #1A1A24. Measured contrast is about 3.1:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text.
strings.issue:NMB-111:desc:1: Those labels must meet AA in both themes. Primary numbers are fine; only the secondary line fails. Light mode already passes at 5.2:1.
strings.issue:NMB-111:desc:2: Token color.text.muted was tuned for light backgrounds and reused as-is for dark. Splitting a color.text.muted.dark near #B0B0C0 or lifting the dark muted step one level should clear the audit without washing out the hierarchy.
strings.issue:NMB-112:title: Mention autocomplete inserts an extra space before the handle
strings.issue:NMB-112:desc:0: Typing @ in the editor opens mention autocomplete. Choosing a person inserts @handle but with an extra leading space when the caret was already after a space, producing two spaces before the at-sign.
strings.issue:NMB-112:desc:1: Insertion should replace the trigger query with a single mention node and at most one separating space from the preceding word. The double space shows up in rendered comments and in notification previews as an awkward gap.
strings.issue:NMB-112:desc:2: Mention plugin insertMention always prepends a space text node for word boundary, ignoring that the delete range already consumed a trailing space from the query. Reopened after the first fix only covered mid-word triggers, not triggers that start after punctuation-plus-space.
strings.issue:NMB-113:title: Kanban column counts ignore cards moved via keyboard shortcuts
strings.issue:NMB-113:desc:0: Kanban column headers show a live card count. Dragging a card with the mouse updates both source and destination counts immediately. Moving a card with keyboard shortcuts (Focus card then Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Arrow) updates the card position but leaves the header counts unchanged until a full board refresh.
strings.issue:NMB-113:desc:1: Counts should stay consistent regardless of input method. Keyboard moves go through board.moveCard which updates column arrays but skips the columnMeta.counts reducer that the drag-end path calls.
strings.issue:NMB-113:desc:2: Teams that rely on keyboard navigation for accessibility see wrong WIP totals and sometimes pull more work into a column that already looks full by count. Aligning the keyboard path with the same count mutation as pointer drag should close the gap.
strings.issue:NMB-114:title: Date picker shifts one day backward in Pacific/Auckland timezone
strings.issue:NMB-114:desc:0: Users with browser timezone Pacific/Auckland who pick a calendar date on dashboard filter widgets (due date, created range) get a stored ISO date one calendar day earlier than the day they clicked.
strings.issue:NMB-114:desc:1: Selecting 15 March should store 2026-03-15. Instead the control emits 2026-03-14T11:00:00.000Z and the chip displays 14 March after reopening the picker.
strings.issue:NMB-114:desc:2: Conversion runs Date.UTC(y, m, d) after reading local Y/M/D, but an intermediate new Date(y, m, d) is serialized via toISOString() before the UTC rebuild, which shifts the day for UTC+12/+13 offsets. Building a plain date string YYYY-MM-DD without a Date instance until the API boundary would avoid the skew.
strings.issue:NMB-115:title: Export CSV truncates multi-line description fields at 255 characters
strings.issue:NMB-115:desc:0: Board and issue CSV exports cut multi-line description fields at 255 characters even when the source field holds several kilobytes. Single-line short descriptions export in full.
strings.issue:NMB-115:desc:1: Full description text should appear in the CSV cell with embedded newlines escaped per RFC 4180. Importers downstream lose acceptance criteria and repro steps that live past the 255th character.
strings.issue:NMB-115:desc:2: Export worker still applies a legacy VARCHAR(255) style truncate from the old MySQL report schema; the truncate happens in CsvRowMapper.mapDescription before quoting. Removing that cap or raising it to the same 32KB limit as the API would match product expectations.
strings.issue:NMB-116:title: Sidebar badge count freezes after dismissing the last unread item
strings.issue:NMB-116:desc:0: The sidebar notifications badge shows the unread count. Opening the panel and dismissing the final unread item clears the list UI, but the badge number stays at 1 (or whatever it was) until logout or hard reload.
strings.issue:NMB-116:desc:1: Badge should hit zero when unread drops to zero. The dismiss mutation removed the item from the list query but never wrote unreadCount: 0 into the badge cache entry.
strings.issue:NMB-116:desc:2: Stale badge makes people keep opening an empty inbox. Fix was to invalidate notifications.unreadCount on every mark-read/dismiss and to derive the badge from that query only.
strings.issue:NMB-117:title: Billing portal redirect loops when the customer already has a portal session
strings.issue:NMB-117:desc:0: From Billing settings, Manage payment methods should send the user to the hosted billing portal once. If the customer already has an open portal session created in the last ~30 minutes, our backend still requests a new session URL, then the portal responds with a redirect back to our return_url, which immediately requests another session — an infinite loop between app and portal.
strings.issue:NMB-117:desc:1: Expected: reuse the active portal session or show an in-app message that a portal tab is already open. Actual: browser spins until the tab is killed; some users report 20+ hops in a few seconds.
strings.issue:NMB-117:desc:2: Session create endpoint ignores billing_portal_sessions.active for the customer id and always POSTs a fresh session. Portal then rejects the duplicate with a redirect to return_url without a session token, and our page treats that as needs portal again. Short-circuit when an unexpired session row exists.
strings.issue:NMB-118:title: Editor collaborative cursors jump to line zero after a paste of 500+ lines
strings.issue:NMB-118:desc:0: In a multiplayer editor session, remote collaborative cursors jump to line 0 (document start) immediately after any participant pastes a block of roughly 500 lines or more. Local caret stays correct; only remote presence positions break.
strings.issue:NMB-118:desc:1: Remote cursors should re-map through the same transform as the paste transaction. After a large paste they all collapse to position 0 until the next small edit, which confuses co-authors about who is where.
strings.issue:NMB-118:desc:2: Presence positions were mapped with a stepwise transform walk that bailed out when the step count exceeded 256, returning a null map that defaulted to 0. Raising the limit and batching paste as a single ReplaceStep fixed the jump.
strings.issue:NMB-119:title: Saved view filters apply only the first three selected components
strings.issue:NMB-119:desc:0: Saved views on the dashboard can include multiple component filters. When a view is saved with four or more components selected, only the first three are applied when the view is loaded; the rest are silently dropped from the active filter state (though still visible as selected in the edit dialog until save).
strings.issue:NMB-119:desc:1: All selected components should participate in the query. Boards filtered by four components show a superset of cards because the fourth filter never reaches GET /issues.
strings.issue:NMB-119:desc:2: The saved-view JSON schema used components as a fixed string array of length 3 from an early product limit. The UI allowed more selections but serialization truncated with slice(0, 3). Schema and mapper now accept up to 25 components.
strings.issue:NMB-12:title: Remember the last used onboarding checklist per workspace
strings.issue:NMB-12:desc:0: Context: Remember the last used onboarding checklist per workspace.
strings.issue:NMB-12:desc:1: Acceptance: behaviour is covered by a test and documented in the reference.
strings.issue:NMB-120:title: Notification preferences toggle reverts after navigating away within 2 seconds
strings.issue:NMB-120:desc:0: On Notification preferences, flipping a channel toggle (email, in-app, mobile) shows the optimistic ON/OFF state, but if the user navigates to another settings section within about two seconds the toggle reverts to the previous value on return. Waiting longer than two seconds before navigating persists correctly.
strings.issue:NMB-120:desc:1: A successful preference change should survive navigation immediately. The PATCH to /users/me/notification-preferences is debounced at 2000ms; unmounting the form aborts the debounced write without a flush.
strings.issue:NMB-120:desc:2: Reopened: the first patch flushed on unmount for email toggles only; in-app and mobile still use a shared debounce timer that is cleared in cleanup without invoking the pending callback.
strings.issue:NMB-121:title: Dashboard heatmap cells render transparent under forced colors mode
strings.issue:NMB-121:desc:0: Dashboard activity heatmaps look correct in normal themes. Under Windows forced colors / high-contrast mode (or forced-colors: active), every cell paints fully transparent so the grid is an empty frame with axis labels only.
strings.issue:NMB-121:desc:1: Cells must remain distinguishable in forced colors, typically via system color pairs (Canvas / Highlight) or explicit forced-color-adjust handling. Currently fill comes from CSS variables that resolve to transparent when the browser overrides the palette.
strings.issue:NMB-121:desc:2: Heatmap cells set background-color to var(--heat-n) without a forced-colors fallback, and forced-color-adjust: none was never set. Adding system-color borders and a non-transparent fallback fill restored the grid for high-contrast users.
strings.issue:NMB-122:title: OAuth callback lands on the root dashboard instead of the deep-linked board
strings.issue:NMB-122:desc:0: Starting OAuth from a deep link such as /boards/42?card=881 should return the user to that board and card after the IdP round-trip. After callback the app lands on / (root dashboard) and the original path is discarded.
strings.issue:NMB-122:desc:1: Post-login routing must restore returnTo from the pre-auth state. The authorize redirect stored returnTo in sessionStorage under a key that the callback page no longer reads after the auth package split.
strings.issue:NMB-122:desc:2: Users opening notification emails lose context and have to hunt for the card. Restoring returnTo from the signed state parameter (already round-tripped to the IdP) fixed deep links without relying on sessionStorage.
strings.issue:NMB-123:title: Bulk archive leaves orphaned cards visible until the next poll cycle
strings.issue:NMB-123:desc:0: Bulk archive from the list multi-select removes cards from the server and shows a success toast, but the archived cards remain visible on the board until the next poll (default 30s) or a manual refresh.
strings.issue:NMB-123:desc:1: Optimistic removal should drop those card ids from the board store immediately. The bulk archive mutation updates the list query cache but not the kanban column entity map, so the board keeps rendering orphans that 404 when opened.
strings.issue:NMB-123:desc:2: Clicking an orphan opens an error empty state. Syncing board cache eviction with the same id list passed to POST /issues/bulk-archive will clear them without waiting for poll.
strings.issue:NMB-124:title: Search result snippets strip HTML entities incorrectly for ampersands
strings.issue:NMB-124:desc:0: Global search snippets that contain HTML entities for ampersands display wrong. A title stored as R&D roadmap becomes R&amp;D roadmap in the snippet, or sometimes R&D with a stripped character depending on the path.
strings.issue:NMB-124:desc:1: Snippets should decode entities once and show a single ampersand. Double-encoding happens because the search indexer escapes HTML before Elasticsearch, and the snippet highlighter escapes again when building highlight.fragments.
strings.issue:NMB-124:desc:2: Readers scanning results for partner names with ampersands waste time opening the wrong hits. Decode before highlight, or mark fragments as already safe and skip the second escape.
strings.issue:NMB-125:title: Editor undo stack collapses multiple keystrokes into a single step after idle
strings.issue:NMB-125:desc:0: Editor undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) normally reverses one logical typing burst. After the user pauses longer than the idle merge window (~800ms) and types again, several distinct keystrokes from the new burst are later undone as a single step, so undo removes more text than expected.
strings.issue:NMB-125:desc:1: Each continuous typing segment after an idle gap should become its own history item. The history plugin resets the merge timer on idle but reuses the same transaction group id when focus never left the doc, so the next characters join the previous closed step.
strings.issue:NMB-125:desc:2: Writers who undo carefully lose whole words instead of the last character. Generating a new history group id whenever the idle timer fires would restore per-burst undo.
strings.issue:NMB-126:title: Invoice line items show tax twice when the workspace uses reverse charge
strings.issue:NMB-126:desc:0: For workspaces with reverse charge VAT enabled, invoice PDFs and the Billing → Invoices detail view show tax amount both as a line-item tax column and again as a separate reverse-charge tax row, effectively doubling the tax display (totals remain correct because one row is a display-only annotation).
strings.issue:NMB-126:desc:1: Reverse charge invoices should show tax as 0 on lines with a single reverse-charge note, not tax twice. Finance partners flagged PDF exports as non-compliant for their records.
strings.issue:NMB-126:desc:2: Invoice builder applied the standard tax decorator and the reverse-charge decorator without mutual exclusion. Guarding the standard tax column when tax.regime === reverse_charge removed the duplicate.
strings.issue:NMB-127:title: Avatar upload accepts HEIC files but serves a broken placeholder image
strings.issue:NMB-127:desc:0: Profile avatar upload accepts .heic / .heif (file picker and drag-drop), returns 201, and shows a progress complete state. The served avatar URL then returns a 1x1 broken placeholder PNG instead of a converted image.
strings.issue:NMB-127:desc:1: Either reject HEIC client-side with a clear message, or transcode to JPEG/WebP on upload and serve that. Today we accept the file, store the original bytes, and the image pipeline fails conversion without failing the upload.
strings.issue:NMB-127:desc:2: Workers log heic decode not available in this runtime then write the placeholder. Users on iPhone cameras think their photo is set until everyone else sees the broken icon.
strings.issue:NMB-128:title: Pinned comment markers disappear when the document is reopened in split view
strings.issue:NMB-128:desc:0: Pinned comment markers (gutter icons that jump to a pinned thread) show correctly in single-pane editor. Opening the same document in split view (two panes, same doc id) causes all pinned markers to disappear in both panes until the document is closed and opened again in single view.
strings.issue:NMB-128:desc:1: Markers should remain bound to document positions independent of pane count. Split view mounts a second EditorView that re-inits plugin state from an empty pin list because the pin plugin keys state by view instance rather than document id.
strings.issue:NMB-128:desc:2: Reviewers who use split to compare sections lose pin navigation. Sharing pin plugin state across views for the same doc id should keep markers visible.
strings.issue:NMB-129:title: Dashboard refresh button triggers two identical network requests in Firefox
strings.issue:NMB-129:desc:0: Clicking the dashboard Refresh control in Firefox fires two identical GETs to the same metrics endpoint within a few milliseconds (e.g. two GET /api/v2/dashboard/summary with the same query string). Chrome and Safari fire one.
strings.issue:NMB-129:desc:1: A single click should produce one network request. Double fetch wastes quota on heavy summary queries and can flicker widgets that reset loading state twice.
strings.issue:NMB-129:desc:2: Firefox delivers both the click handler and a residual keyup-as-click on the focused button when Space was used earlier to focus it; the handler is not idempotent. Guarding with an in-flight ref or listening only to click with preventDefault on key repeat should make Firefox match other browsers.
strings.issue:NMB-13:title: Instrument SSO callback with structured logs
strings.issue:NMB-13:desc:0: Context: Instrument SSO callback with structured logs.
strings.issue:NMB-13:desc:1: Acceptance: behaviour is covered by a test and documented in the reference.
strings.issue:NMB-130:title: Login form submits twice if Enter is pressed while the request is in flight
strings.issue:NMB-130:desc:0: On the login form, submitting with Enter while the first /auth/login request is still in flight sends a second identical POST. Both can succeed and create two session rows, or the second fails with 409 and surfaces a misleading error over the successful login.
strings.issue:NMB-130:desc:1: While a login attempt is pending, further submits (button or Enter) must be ignored. The button disables on click but the form onSubmit still accepts Enter because disabled is only on the button, not a submitting flag on the form.
strings.issue:NMB-130:desc:2: Duplicate sessions confuse session management and rate limits. A isSubmitting guard at the form level before calling the auth client fixes the double POST.
strings.issue:NMB-131:title: Notification email subject line drops non-ASCII characters from the issue title
strings.issue:NMB-131:desc:0: Notification emails whose issue titles include non-ASCII characters (e.g. accented names, CJK, emoji) arrive with those characters missing from the subject line. Body content retains the correct title.
strings.issue:NMB-131:desc:1: Subject should preserve the same Unicode as the issue title. The mailer builds subjects with an ASCII-only header encoder path that strips bytes outside 0x20-0x7E instead of applying RFC 2047 encoded-words.
strings.issue:NMB-131:desc:2: Recipients scanning inbox subjects cannot identify issues with localized titles. Switching subject encoding to UTF-8 encoded-word (or letting the ESP handle Unicode subjects) restores the full title.
strings.issue:NMB-132:title: Board filter URL params are lost when opening a card in a new tab
strings.issue:NMB-132:desc:0: When a board is filtered (e.g. assignee=me and status=in_progress in the query string), using Open in new tab on a card preserves only /cards/{id} and drops the filter query string from the opener URL context. That is expected for the card URL, but the parent board tab also rewrites its history to strip filter params when the context menu open fires.
strings.issue:NMB-132:desc:1: Opening a card in a new tab should not mutate the source board filter URL. The board route listens to a global card:open event and calls setSearchParams with only card, wiping other params.
strings.issue:NMB-132:desc:2: People lose multi-filter setups after middle-clicking a card and have to re-apply filters. Scope the param write to the new tab navigation target only, not the opener history.
strings.issue:NMB-133:title: Editor table column resize snaps to zero width on the last column
strings.issue:NMB-133:desc:0: In the editor table UI, dragging the resize handle on the last column snaps that column width to 0px on mouseup if the drag ends within 4px of the table right edge. Other columns resize smoothly.
strings.issue:NMB-133:desc:1: Last column should clamp to a minimum width (currently 48px for others) like every other column. The last handle max delta is computed against container width minus prior columns, but the clamp runs before subtracting scrollbar width (12-16px), so the allowed width becomes negative and snaps to zero.
strings.issue:NMB-133:desc:2: Tables with a collapsed last column hide cell content and are hard to recover without undo. Applying the same min-width clamp after scrollbar compensation keeps the last column visible.
strings.issue:NMB-134:title: Billing usage meter shows negative remaining seats after a plan downgrade
strings.issue:NMB-134:desc:0: After downgrading a workspace plan (e.g. Business 25 seats to Team 10 seats) while 14 seats are still assigned, the Billing usage meter shows -4 seats remaining instead of 0 remaining and 4 over limit.
strings.issue:NMB-134:desc:1: Remaining seats should floor at zero with a separate overage indicator when active members exceed the new plan cap. Negative remaining confuses admins into thinking the meter is broken and blocks the correct upgrade CTA copy.
strings.issue:NMB-134:desc:2: Meter computes plan.seats - members.active without clamping; the downgrade webhook updates plan.seats before seat reclamation finishes. Display should use Math.max(0, plan.seats - members.active) and surface overBy when negative.
strings.issue:NMB-135:title: Keyboard focus trap on the workspace invite modal cannot be dismissed with Esc
strings.issue:NMB-135:desc:0: The workspace invite modal traps focus for keyboard users as intended, but pressing Escape does not close it. Overlay click and the X button still work.
strings.issue:NMB-135:desc:1: Escape should dismiss the modal and restore focus to the Invite trigger. The dialog registers a keydown listener on the modal node only; when focus is inside a nested focusable (email input), the event does not bubble to that listener because stopPropagation runs on the input enter-to-add-chip handler for all keys.
strings.issue:NMB-135:desc:2: Keyboard-only admins cannot bail out without Tabbing to the close control. Moving Escape handling to document while the modal is mounted (and ignoring it when a nested popover is open) restores expected dialog behavior.
strings.issue:NMB-136:title: Dashboard empty state illustration flashes on every data refetch
strings.issue:NMB-136:desc:0: On dashboards that already have data, each background refetch briefly mounts the empty-state illustration (cloud with No activity yet) for a flash before the loaded data paints again. First load empty state is correct when there is truly no data.
strings.issue:NMB-136:desc:1: Refetch should keep showing the previous data or a subtle loading affordance, not the empty illustration. The query sets data to undefined while isFetching is true because keepPreviousData / placeholderData is not enabled on the summary query.
strings.issue:NMB-136:desc:2: The flash is distracting on 15s polling and looks like a reliability bug. Enabling placeholder previous data (or gating empty state on isLoading && !data) removes the flicker.
strings.issue:NMB-137:title: SSO login fails when the IdP returns a NameID with mixed case domain
